title: processkit-cli `probe --json` compatibility report
description: The single JSON line `processkit-cli probe --json` prints to stdout — the fail-closed launcher preflight a consumer runs on a candidate binary before launching anything through it. Printed in both the compatible and the incompatible case (an unmet `--require-*` expectation exits PROBE_INCOMPATIBLE (110) with `compatible: false`), so the consumer always has a parseable result. The normative prose is docs/compatibility.md and docs/integration.md, "Fail-closed preflight"; the in-code source of truth is src/probe.rs. Validated against fixtures/schema/cli/probe.jsonl, and against the real binary's output, by tests/machine_output.rs.

probe_version.description: The report's own format version (src/probe.rs, PROBE_VERSION) — the launcher contract's own axis, independent of the JSONL `schema_version`, the control-plane `snapshot_version`, and the `registry_version`. Pinned here: a bump is a breaking change to this shape and updates this document with it.

binary.description: The binary's package name, so a consumer can confirm the candidate really is this runner and not some other program that happens to accept a `probe` argument.

version.description: The binary's semantic version (CARGO_PKG_VERSION). Together with `surface`, this is what a consumer pins for the outputs that carry no version field of their own (fixtures/schema/cli/README.md, "Versioning").

schema_version.description: The JSONL event `schema_version` this binary emits — the value adapters pin (docs/schema.md, "Versioning"). Currently 1.

exit_code_band.description: The reserved runner exit-code band this binary uses (docs/exit-codes.md). A consumer pins it so a child exit that happens to fall in the band is never confused with a runner failure. Currently 100-119.

surface.description: The CLI surface tokens this binary exposes: every subcommand name plus `<subcommand>:--<long-flag>` for each of its long flags, sorted and deduplicated. Derived from the live clap definition, so it cannot drift from the real parser; clap's own `--help`/`--version` are excluded. A third, deliberately distinct form — `<subcommand>:<capability>`, with **no** `--` — names a platform capability rather than a spelling the parser accepts: `attest:peer-identity` is present exactly where this build can obtain a kernel-authenticated identity for a control-plane client, which is what makes `attest` able to return a verdict at all (docs/integration.md §1; src/probe.rs, PEER_IDENTITY_TOKEN). A consumer requires it with the same `--require-surface` as any flag and gets the same fail-closed 110 when it is absent; the missing `--` is what keeps the two categories from being read as one another.

compatible.description: Whether every `--require-*` expectation the consumer asked for is satisfied. `true` when none was requested (a healthy self-report).

mismatches.description: One human-readable reason per unmet expectation — the parseable "why" behind `compatible: false`. Always present; empty exactly when `compatible` is true.

then.description: A compatible report never carries a mismatch: `compatible` is exactly `mismatches.is_empty()` (src/probe.rs, `run`).

else.description: An incompatible report always names at least one concrete reason — never a generic failure.
